claim: Let \(k=\mathbb F_q\) have characteristic \(p\), with \(q=p^e\), and let \(I\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\) be a proper zero-dimensional monomial ideal. Let \(S=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^d:x^\alpha\notin I\}\), \(N=|S|\), and \(s_r=|\{\alpha\in S:p^r\alpha\in S\}|\) for \(r\ge0\). For \(R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/I\), the number of units satisfying \(u^{p^r}=1\) is \(q^{N-s_r}\). With \(K_r=e(N-s_r)\) and \(m_r=2K_r-K_{r-1}-K_{r+1}\) for \(r\ge1\), the full unit group is \(R^\times\cong C_{q-1}\times \prod_{r\ge1}C_{p^r}^{m_r}\), with only finitely many nonzero \(m_r\).
scientific_limitations: Applies to finite-dimensional commutative monomial quotients over finite fields.
Does not claim a formula for arbitrary nonmonomial or noncommutative finite local algebras.
A broader published theorem may imply the formula; the literature search was not exhaustive.
title: Frobenius-dilation formula for unit groups of finite monomial algebras
